tasks.short: Collate report pages and attachments into complete, correctly ordered document sets.

steps.what: Collect report pages, attachments and assembly instructions.
Arrange pages and attachments in the required sequence.
Check completeness, page sequence and attachment versions.
Assemble paper sets and insert physical attachments where requested.
Save the checked document with its version and assembly reference.

tasks.design: A configured intake in the {DOCS} collects versioned sources and an assembly manifest. A deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} orders pages, checks counts and duplicates, and presents exceptions before saving the checked document in the {DOCS}; physical inserts remain a handling task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources arrived separately, naming was inconsistent, and assembly instructions were rarely captured as reusable rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls and inexpensive assembly scripts can handle repeatable packets. AI coding can reduce implementation effort without changing the underlying page-handling technology.
tasks.still_hard: A complete manifest can still describe the wrong source version. Unnumbered scans, foldouts and physical attachments require inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when a technically complete packet is inappropriate for its intended reader, and resolve conflicting source versions.

ambition.what: Offer a pre-meeting document-pack completeness check.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from page handling to resolving incomplete packets before deadlines. The person gains authority to return incomplete submissions against an agreed checklist, not to approve their substantive content.

reach.task: Prepare decision packs for project checkpoints.
reach.learn: Learn checkpoint requirements, document dependencies and submission cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Page assembly, manifest checks and versioned filing can use deterministic document processing.
Physical inserts and ambiguous versions limit fully unattended collation.

assumptions: Time shares describe a mixed digital and paper workload, not measured customer timings.
Most packets have an explicit page order or reusable section sequence.
The prior's large gathering share falls when assembly instructions identify source locations.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a narrow pilot; shared components overlap with other tasks.
unknowns: How much work still requires paper sets or physical inserts?
Does the {DOCS} expose stable version identifiers and supported access?
Who resolves conflicting versions and owns the assembly checklist?
What consultation is required under national rules for the proposed workflow?
research_questions: Can manifest checks detect missing, repeated and superseded pages across representative packets?
How much inspection remains after routine packets use governed source folders?
new_work: Maintain packet manifests and section-order rules.
Review missing-page, duplicate and version exceptions.
Check access permissions and failed assembly jobs.

tasks.short: Reformat documents by applying styles and moving paragraphs or columns to the requested layout.

steps.what: Read the document and requested layout changes.
Apply paragraph styles, margins, headings and column settings.
Move specified paragraphs, tables and columns into their required positions.
Inspect page breaks, reading order, tables and content preservation.
Save the checked version and return its reference.

tasks.design: Governed templates in the {DOCS} apply standard styles, while a deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} moves explicitly identified content blocks. Content comparisons and rendered previews support a focused layout review before the checked version is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents relied on manual spacing and inconsistent styles. Layout requests often referred to positions rather than stable section identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Template configuration handles routine formatting, and small scripts can preserve and relocate structured content. AI coding makes format adapters cheaper to build, although unusual layouts still need review.
tasks.still_hard: Floating objects, damaged files, complex tables and vague instructions can defeat reliable transformations. Automated content checks do not establish good visual hierarchy.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret the reader's needs and choose a clear layout when instructions allow several reasonable arrangements.
tasks.altitude: The person spends more time reviewing difficult layouts and improving templates. They can select approved layout patterns and reject unclear instructions; document owners retain content decisions.

reach.task: Maintain accessible templates for recurring reports and correspondence.
reach.learn: Learn heading structure, reading order, table accessibility and template change control.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx supports governed template-based layout generation; this supports the template approach, not arbitrary document conversion.
Styles, explicit block moves and content comparisons can be implemented without a model loop.

assumptions: Routine requests identify the content to move; ambiguous requests remain human work.
Source documents usually contain editable text rather than scans.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The high automation prior is moderated by rendered-layout inspection and irregular source files.
unknowns: Which document formats and layout features occur most often?
Are approved templates and stable section identifiers available?
Which accessibility requirements apply to the outputs?
What access and consultation are required under national rules?
research_questions: Which layout transformations preserve text, tables, links and reading order reliably?
How often do explicit transformation rules cover incoming requests without interpretation?
new_work: Maintain templates and supported transformation rules.
Review visual previews and content differences.
Handle unsupported objects and ambiguous move instructions.
Retest representative documents after rendering or template changes.

tasks.short: Produce typed correspondence and reports from drafts, corrections, recordings and previous versions.

steps.what: Collect source material, the previous version and document instructions.
Ask the document owner about unclear wording or conflicting instructions.
Copy reusable text and enter explicit corrections from previous versions.
Transcribe remaining handwritten text, recordings or dictation into the draft.

loop.input: Untranscribed source pages or audio segments, with explicit corrections and a controlled terminology list.
loop.output: Source-aligned text with page or time references and marked uncertain passages.
loop.check: Check segment coverage, source alignment and unexplained repetition; a person checks uncertainty, names, numbers and instructions against the source.
loop.stop: At most two passes per page or audio segment and a fixed document processing budget; unresolved passages go to manual transcription.
loop.why_not_simpler: Direct text reuse and explicit edit rules cannot interpret handwriting or speech. Use configured recognition first and restrict the loop to unresolved passages.

steps.what: Compare the draft with sources and correct transcription errors.
Approve the wording and intended use of the checked draft.
File the approved version and its source references.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} retains source versions while deterministic tools reuse existing text, apply explicit edits and generate the document. Configured recognition and a bounded extraction loop handle remaining handwriting or speech, with source-linked review and document-owner approval before the approved version is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed source formats, poor recordings and informal corrections made reliable conversion difficult. Earlier tools often separated recognition from revision and approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Recognition is readily available, while source alignment, document comparison and approval can be connected with small integrations. Better assembly reduces retyping even where recognition quality has not improved.
tasks.still_hard: Names, numbers, accents, overlapping speech and illegible handwriting remain costly to verify. Fluent text can conceal omissions or invented wording.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve the author's intended meaning without silently rewriting it, and recognise passages whose consequences warrant careful confirmation.

ambition.what: Provide reviewed dictation-to-document support for staff who struggle with written input.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving uncertain passages and helping authors express decisions clearly. The person can stop a draft with unresolved source conflicts; the author retains authority over its meaning and use.

reach.task: Turn dictated decisions into reviewed correspondence.
reach.learn: Learn audience requirements, confidentiality handling and decision-confirmation practices.

evidence.claim: Amberscript offers machine transcription and human-checked transcription.
A published study documents invented phrases in speech-to-text output, supporting source-based review.
Digital text reuse and explicit corrections can use deterministic processing before recognition is considered.

assumptions: The step shares represent the source mix across the workload; individual documents may skip reuse or transcription.
Sources may be processed for this purpose under an established GDPR basis.
The workflow prepares documents and does not make decisions about people.
The EU AI Act applies according to the system's intended use; ordinary transcription alone does not establish a high-risk employment use.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates; no vendor accuracy claim is used as a customer forecast.
unknowns: Which languages, recording conditions and handwriting styles occur?
What proportion of work already contains reusable digital text?
Are source recordings authorised, and what retention periods apply?
May source material leave the existing processing environment?
What employee consultation is required under national rules?
research_questions: How often do names, numbers or omitted passages survive the proposed review process?
Does a bounded correction pass improve source fidelity enough to justify its cost?
Which source types should bypass recognition and go directly to manual transcription?
new_work: Review uncertain passages and consequential wording against sources.
Maintain terminology lists and extraction instructions.
Manage source access, retention and approved processing arrangements.
Sample apparently clean transcripts for hidden omissions or invented text.
Handle failed recognition and requests for author clarification.

tasks.short: Maintain records of completed typing work, document references, effort and outstanding corrections.

steps.what: Gather completed document references and assignment details.
Enter completion dates, document references, quantities and status in the work register.
Record effort and explain unusual work or unfinished corrections.
Reconcile missing or duplicate work records against document history.
Send a summary of completed work and outstanding corrections.

tasks.design: Completion events from the {DOCS} populate a configured work register in the {WORKFLOW}, removing separate gathering and re-entry. Rules reconcile document identifiers and status changes, while people declare effort and explain exceptions; the {WORKFLOW} produces an aggregate queue summary for the administrative supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document history and the work register were separate, and assignment identifiers were inconsistent. Effort and completion were often recorded together by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, event triggers and stable document identifiers can capture completion once. Small deterministic integrations can reconcile status without interpreting employee activity.
tasks.still_hard: A saved document is not necessarily completed work. Event timestamps cannot establish effort, and reopened assignments need clear counting rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why work took an unusual path and distinguish genuine completion from a file update.

ambition.what: Review queue priorities each day using overdue assignments and correction backlogs.

tasks.altitude: The person spends less time reconstructing activity and more time resolving stalled assignments. They gain authority to flag and propose daily priority changes; the administrative supervisor retains staffing and performance decisions.

reach.learn: Learn queue ageing, service commitments and how to distinguish demand from rework.

evidence.claim: Completion metadata, duplicate checks and aggregate summaries can use configured workflows and deterministic rules.
In the Netherlands, per-clerk speed or touchless dashboards require works-council consent under the cited provision.
Document timestamps alone do not reliably measure human effort.

assumptions: A shared workbook is the baseline work register; customers already using a records app may need configuration only.
The document-heavy prior is adjusted because maintaining the record usually occurs in a register.
The register tracks assignments and declared effort; it does not infer working time from computer activity.
GDPR requirements apply to identifiable work records; national rules determine additional consultation requirements.
Build ranges are working-day estimates, and consultation lead time may exceed implementation time.
unknowns: Is the current register in the {SPREADSHEET}, {PROJECT} or another supported slot?
What makes an assignment complete, reopened or cancelled?
Are records used for billing, payroll, performance assessment or statutory evidence?
Can the {DOCS} emit completion events with stable assignment identifiers?
Which employee representatives, access owners and retention rules apply?
research_questions: Can completion events reconcile with the existing register without creating duplicate work counts?
Which fields need personal declaration rather than automatic capture?
Would an aggregate queue summary answer the supervisor's operational questions?
new_work: Maintain completion definitions and identifier mappings.
Review unmatched events, duplicates and reopened assignments.
Declare effort and explain unusual work.
Maintain access, retention and employee consultation arrangements.
Monitor failed event delivery and reconcile missed updates.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward document quality, source clarification and service coordination. The person can return incomplete submissions and select approved templates; authors retain content approval, and managers retain staffing decisions.
reach: Prepare project checkpoint packs with project management specialists.
Maintain accessible document templates with administrative assistants.
Support reviewed dictation with executive administrative assistants.
Propose queue priorities with administrative services managers.
skills_to_grow: Document metadata, version control and retention
role.ambitious_version: Run a document-readiness service that checks source completeness, produces accessible drafts and resolves exceptions before authors approve their use.
